subject: general
question: Which book of poems was written by Sarojini Naidu and published in 1905?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The Golden Threshold**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Golden Threshold** is a famous collection of poems written by **Sarojini Naidu** and was first published in **1905** in **London**.
 
• This volume marked her debut in the literary world and established her reputation as a major poet, eventually earning her the title of the **"Nightingale of India"** (**Bharat Kokila**).
 
• The book is divided into three sections: **Folk Songs**, **Songs for Music**, and **Poems**. It features iconic poems like **"Palanquin Bearers"**, **"Coromandel Fishers"**, and **"The Bazaars of Hyderabad"**.
 
• The introduction to the **1905** edition was written by **Arthur Symons**, a renowned British poet and critic, who praised the authentic Indian essence of her work.
 
• The title of the book, **The Golden Threshold**, is also the name of the residence of **Sarojini Naidu** in **Hyderabad**, which is now a center for arts and communication under the **University of Hyderabad**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Indian War of Independence**:

 
 
• This book was authored by **Vinayak Damodar Savarkar** (**V.D. Savarkar**) in **1909**.
 
• It provided a nationalist interpretation of the **Revolt of 1857**, describing it as the **"First War of Indian Independence"** rather than a mere sepoy mutiny.
 
• The book was **banned** by the **British authorities** even before its publication due to its revolutionary content.
 
 
 
• **The Story of My Deportation**:
 
 
• This book was written by the prominent nationalist leader **Lala Lajpat Rai**, popularly known as **Punjab Kesari**.
 
• Published in **1908**, it narrates his experiences and observations during his imprisonment and exile in **Mandalay**, **Burma**, following his arrest in **1907**.
 
 
 
• **Glimpses of World History**:
 
 
• Written by **Jawaharlal Nehru**, this work is a collection of **196 letters** written to his daughter, **Indira Gandhi**, between **1930** and **1933** from various prisons.
 
• It was published in **1934** and provides a broad, secular, and interconnected view of human history from ancient times to the early **20th century**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sarojini Naidu** was born on **February 13, 1879**, in **Hyderabad**. Her birthday is celebrated as **National Women's Day** in **India**.
 
• She was a trailblazer in Indian politics, becoming the **first Indian woman** to serve as the **President** of the **Indian National Congress** at the **Kanpur Session** in **1925**.
 
• Following India's independence in **1947**, she was appointed as the **Governor** of the **United Provinces** (now **Uttar Pradesh**), making her the **first woman** to hold the office of **Governor** in independent **India**.
 
• Other significant literary works by her include **The Bird of Time** (**1912**), **The Broken Wing** (**1917**), and the posthumously published **The Feather of the Dawn** (**1961**).
 
• She was a key participant in the **Salt Satyagraha** of **1930** and led the protest at the **Dharasana Salt Works** alongside other leaders.
